loci.name: Scripture
loci.tagline: Sola scriptura — the rule of faith and life
loci.overview: The Westminster Standards begin not with God but with Scripture (WCF I), and the order is deliberate.

attributes.name: Sufficiency
attributes.baseline_description: Whatever is necessary for God's glory and human salvation is either expressly stated in Scripture, or may be deduced from it by good and necessary consequence (WCF I.6).

attributes.name: Canon
attributes.baseline_description: The 39 books of the Old Testament and 27 of the New, enumerated in WCF I.2; the Apocrypha is explicitly excluded (I.3).

attributes.name: Authority
attributes.baseline_description: Scripture's authority is grounded in God its author and is sealed to the believer's heart by the inward work of the Holy Spirit bearing witness with and by the Word (WCF I.4-5).

attributes.name: Interpretation
attributes.baseline_description: The infallible rule of interpretation is Scripture itself: when there is a question about the true sense of any passage, it must be searched and known by other places that speak more clearly (WCF I.9).

attributes.name: Necessity
attributes.baseline_description: Although the light of nature and the works of creation manifest God's goodness, wisdom, and power, they are not sufficient to give the knowledge of God and his will necessary for salvation; therefore the Lord committed his revelation wholly unto writing (WCF I.1).

loci.name: God & Decree
loci.tagline: The triune God and his eternal counsel
loci.overview: WCF II-V is the Standards' theology proper: God's being and attributes, the Trinity, the eternal decree, creation, and providence.

attributes.name: Trinity
attributes.baseline_description: One God in three persons; the Son eternally begotten of the Father, the Spirit eternally proceeding from the Father and the Son (WCF II.3).

attributes.name: Order of Decrees
attributes.baseline_description: WCF III's language is deliberately drafted to permit both supra- and infralapsarianism without imposing either.

attributes.name: Extent of Atonement
attributes.baseline_description: Christ purchased redemption only for the elect; the atonement is intended, designed, and applied for the elect alone (WCF III.6, VIII.5, VIII.8).

attributes.name: Reprobation
attributes.baseline_description: God passes by the non-elect and ordains them to dishonour and wrath for their sin (WCF III.7).

attributes.name: Covenant of Redemption
attributes.baseline_description: The Standards affirm the substance of the pactum salutis without the developed apparatus of later federal theologians.

loci.name: Covenant
loci.tagline: Federal theology — works, grace, and the unity of redemption
loci.overview: WCF VII is the Standards' structural hinge between theology proper and Christology.

attributes.name: Number of Covenants
attributes.baseline_description: Two covenants: works with Adam, and grace with Christ and his elect (WCF VII.2-3).

attributes.name: Mosaic Covenant
attributes.baseline_description: The Mosaic dispensation is one administration of the one covenant of grace under the law (WCF VII.5-6).

attributes.name: Children of Believers
attributes.baseline_description: Children of one or both believing parents are in the visible church and receive its sign (WCF XXV.2, XXVIII.4).

attributes.name: Testamental Continuity
attributes.baseline_description: The covenant of grace is one and the same in substance through both testaments, differently administered (WCF VII.6).

loci.name: Christology
loci.tagline: Christ the Mediator — natures, offices, states
loci.overview: WCF VIII integrates the conciliar inheritance with the Reformed doctrine of Christ's offices.

attributes.name: Natures
attributes.baseline_description: Two whole, perfect, and distinct natures inseparably joined in one person, without conversion, composition, or confusion (WCF VIII.2).

attributes.name: Offices
attributes.baseline_description: Three offices answering to the three deficiencies of fallen humanity (WCF VIII.1; LC Q. 42-45; SC Q. 23-26).

attributes.name: States & Descent
attributes.baseline_label: Humiliation And Exaltation; No Local Descent
attributes.baseline_description: Two states, humiliation and exaltation; the descendit is interpreted as the continued state of death between cross and resurrection.

attributes.name: Active-Obedience Imputation
attributes.baseline_description: Both Christ's obedience and his sacrifice are imputed to the justified believer (WCF VIII.5; XI.1, 3).

loci.name: Soteriology
loci.tagline: The application of redemption — calling, justifying, sanctifying
loci.overview: WCF X-XVIII traces the ordo salutis from effectual calling through assurance.

attributes.name: Effectual Calling
attributes.baseline_description: The Spirit effectually calls the elect by enlightening their minds, renewing their wills, and drawing them to Christ (WCF X.1-2).

attributes.name: Justification Ground
attributes.baseline_description: Justification is a forensic act grounded in the imputation of Christ's whole obedience and satisfaction, received by faith alone (WCF XI.1-4).

attributes.name: Saving Faith
attributes.baseline_description: Saving faith receives and rests upon Christ alone for salvation, as he is offered in the gospel (WCF XIV.2; SC Q. 86).

attributes.name: Perseverance
attributes.baseline_description: Those accepted in Christ, effectually called, and sanctified by his Spirit can neither totally nor finally fall away from grace (WCF XVII.1).

attributes.name: Assurance
attributes.baseline_label: Attainable But Not Essence Of Faith
attributes.baseline_description: Infallible assurance is attainable in this life but does not belong to the essence of faith (WCF XVIII.3).

loci.name: Law & Sanctification
loci.tagline: The moral law, the Sabbath, the Christian life
loci.overview: WCF XIX-XXII handles the law, Christian liberty, worship and Sabbath, and lawful oaths and vows.

attributes.name: Uses of the Law
attributes.baseline_description: Civil, pedagogical, and normative uses of the law are affirmed (WCF XIX.5-6).

attributes.name: Tripartite Division
attributes.baseline_description: Moral law remains perpetually binding; judicial law expired with the Jewish polity except for general equity; ceremonial law is abrogated in Christ (WCF XIX.3-5).

attributes.name: Sabbath
attributes.baseline_description: One day in seven is to be kept holy; changed to the first day of the week from the resurrection of Christ (WCF XXI.7-8).

attributes.name: Good Works
attributes.baseline_description: Good works are the fruits and evidences of a true and lively faith; they cannot merit pardon or eternal life (WCF XVI.2, 5).

loci.name: Ecclesiology & Worship
loci.overview: WCF XXV-XXXI plus XXI handle the church, communion of saints, sacraments, worship, discipline, and synods.

attributes.name: Polity
attributes.baseline_description: Christ has instituted a graded series of presbyterial assemblies by divine right.

attributes.name: Sacramental Efficacy
attributes.baseline_label: Signs And Seals Conferring Grace By Spirit
attributes.baseline_description: Sacraments are signs and seals of the covenant of grace, conferring the grace signified by the Spirit and the word of institution upon worthy receivers.

attributes.name: Regulative Principle
attributes.baseline_description: Only what is instituted by God in Scripture may be done in worship (WCF XXI.1).

attributes.name: Censures & Synods
attributes.baseline_description: Admonition, suspension from the sacrament, excommunication, and graded synods are affirmed in the Standards.

loci.name: Civil & Last Things
loci.tagline: Magistrate, oaths, marriage; death, resurrection, judgment
loci.overview: WCF XXIII-XXIV and XXXII-XXXIII frame the Standards' civil and eschatological commitments.

attributes.name: Magistrate's Role
attributes.baseline_description: The 1646 text gives the magistrate duties toward both tables of the Decalogue.

attributes.name: Oaths & Marriage
attributes.baseline_label: Oaths Lawful Serious; Divorce Adultery Or Desertion
attributes.baseline_description: Lawful oaths are a serious part of religious worship; divorce is limited to adultery or willful desertion.

attributes.name: Intermediate State
attributes.baseline_label: Immediate Conscious With God Or Judgment
attributes.baseline_description: Souls of the righteous are immediately received into heaven; souls of the wicked are cast into hell, reserved to judgment (WCF XXXII.1).

attributes.name: Final Judgment
attributes.baseline_description: God has appointed a day wherein he will judge the world in righteousness by Jesus Christ (WCF XXXIII.1-2; SC Q. 38).

doctrine_heads.name: Prolegomena / The Nature of Theology
doctrine_heads.description: The grounds and method of theological knowledge: why theology is necessary, how it differs from philosophy, and what role Scripture plays as the principium cognoscendi of all doctrinal inquiry.

doctrine_heads.name: Of God, and of the Holy Trinity
doctrine_heads.description: The one true and living God: his infinite being, attributes, and the three persons of the Godhead — Father, Son, and Holy Spirit — of one substance, power, and eternity.

doctrine_heads.name: Of God's Eternal Decree
doctrine_heads.description: God's eternal, free, and unchangeable purpose ordaining whatsoever comes to pass, including his predestination of some to everlasting life and his passing by of the rest.

doctrine_heads.name: Of Creation
doctrine_heads.description: God's creation of the world and all things in it, visible and invisible, in the space of six days, and all very good.

doctrine_heads.name: Of Providence
doctrine_heads.description: God's most holy, wise, and powerful preserving and governing of all his creatures and their actions, ordering them to his own glory.

doctrine_heads.name: Of the Fall of Man, of Sin, and of the Punishment thereof
doctrine_heads.description: The fall of our first parents from their original righteousness through the temptation of Satan, the transmission of original sin to all their posterity, and the resulting bondage and punishment of sin.

doctrine_heads.name: Of God's Covenant with Man
doctrine_heads.description: The covenant of works made with Adam and, upon his fall, the covenant of grace freely offered to sinners in Christ, one in substance though variously administered.

doctrine_heads.name: Of Christ the Mediator
doctrine_heads.description: The Son of God, the second person of the Trinity, taking upon himself man's nature to be the only Mediator between God and man, executing the offices of prophet, priest, and king.

doctrine_heads.name: Of Free Will
doctrine_heads.description: The natural liberty of man's will in its fourfold state — innocency, sin, grace, and glory — and its bondage and freedom under each.

doctrine_heads.name: Of Effectual Calling
doctrine_heads.description: God's effectual calling of all those, and those only, whom he has predestined unto life, by his Word and Spirit, out of the state of sin and death.

doctrine_heads.name: Of Justification
doctrine_heads.description: The free act of God's grace in pardoning sin and accepting sinners as righteous, not for anything wrought in them, but for Christ's righteousness imputed and received by faith alone.

doctrine_heads.name: Of Adoption
doctrine_heads.description: The act of God's free grace by which believers are received into the number of, and enjoy the liberties and privileges of, the children of God.

doctrine_heads.name: Of Sanctification
doctrine_heads.description: The real and personal renewal of those effectually called and regenerated, after the image of God, through the sanctifying Spirit and the virtue of Christ's death and resurrection.

doctrine_heads.name: Of Saving Faith
doctrine_heads.description: The grace of faith wrought in the hearts of the elect by the Spirit of God, ordinarily through the ministry of the Word, by which they receive and rest upon Christ alone for salvation.

doctrine_heads.name: Of Repentance unto Life
doctrine_heads.description: The evangelical grace by which a sinner, out of a true sense of sin and apprehension of God's mercy in Christ, grieves for and turns from all his sins unto God.

doctrine_heads.name: Of Good Works
doctrine_heads.description: Good works, done in obedience to God's commandments, as the fruits and evidences of a true and lively faith, which cannot merit pardon of sin or eternal life.

doctrine_heads.name: Of the Perseverance of the Saints
doctrine_heads.description: The certain perseverance of those whom God has accepted in his Beloved, effectually called, and sanctified by his Spirit, who can neither totally nor finally fall away from the state of grace.

doctrine_heads.name: Of the Assurance of Grace and Salvation
doctrine_heads.description: The believer's infallible assurance of being in a state of grace, founded upon the divine truth of the promises of salvation, and attainable without extraordinary revelation.

doctrine_heads.name: Of the Law of God
doctrine_heads.description: The moral law given to Adam as a covenant of works, delivered afterward on Mount Sinai in the ten commandments, and its abiding uses to believers and unbelievers alike.

doctrine_heads.name: Of Christian Liberty, and Liberty of Conscience
doctrine_heads.description: The liberty purchased for believers under the gospel from the guilt of sin, the rigor of the moral law, and the bondage of Satan, together with the liberty of conscience from doctrines and commandments of men.

doctrine_heads.name: Of Religious Worship and the Sabbath-day
doctrine_heads.description: The regulative principle governing acceptable worship of God, and the Sabbath — one day in seven kept holy, changed to the Lord's Day since Christ's resurrection.

doctrine_heads.name: Of Lawful Oaths and Vows
doctrine_heads.description: The lawful use of oaths and vows as a part of religious worship, to be taken with due reverence and in accordance with truth, righteousness, and judgment.

doctrine_heads.name: Of the Civil Magistrate
doctrine_heads.description: God's ordination of civil magistrates for his own glory and the public good, their lawful authority, and the duty of the people to obey them in lawful things.

doctrine_heads.name: Of Marriage and Divorce
doctrine_heads.description: Marriage as instituted between one man and one woman for their mutual help, the propagation of offspring, and the prevention of uncleanness, and the biblical grounds for divorce.

doctrine_heads.name: Of the Church
doctrine_heads.description: The catholic or universal Church, invisible and visible, out of which there is ordinarily no possibility of salvation, and Christ's headship over it.

doctrine_heads.name: Of the Communion of the Saints
doctrine_heads.description: The fellowship believers have with Christ and with one another in grace, gifts, and duties, without infringing upon their rights of property or family.

doctrine_heads.name: Of the Sacraments
doctrine_heads.description: The sacraments as holy signs and seals of the covenant of grace, instituted by God to represent Christ and his benefits and to distinguish the visible church from the world.

doctrine_heads.name: Of Baptism
doctrine_heads.description: Baptism as a sacrament of the new testament, a sign and seal of ingrafting into Christ, to be administered once to a person by water in the name of the Trinity.

doctrine_heads.name: Of the Lord's Supper
doctrine_heads.description: The Lord's Supper as instituted by Christ for the perpetual remembrance of his sacrifice, the spiritual nourishment of believers, and their communion with him and each other.

doctrine_heads.name: Of Church Censures
doctrine_heads.description: The keys of the kingdom of heaven committed to church officers, by which they open and shut the kingdom through censures including admonition, suspension, and excommunication.

doctrine_heads.name: Of Synods and Councils
doctrine_heads.description: The calling of synods and councils for the better government and edification of the church, their proper authority, and the limits of that authority.

doctrine_heads.name: Of the State of Man After Death, and of the Resurrection of the Dead
doctrine_heads.description: The immortality of the soul after death, its immediate entrance into glory or torment, and the resurrection of the bodies of all the dead at the last day.

doctrine_heads.name: Of the Last Judgment
doctrine_heads.description: The day appointed by God in which he will judge the world in righteousness by Jesus Christ, for the manifestation of his mercy and justice, and the everlasting destiny of the righteous and the wicked.
